## formal
Let $A$ be an associative unital ring and $(v_{a}, w_{a})$, $a = 1, \dots, m$, switches in $A$ ($v_{a}^{2} = w_{a}^{2} = 0$, $v_{a}w_{a} + w_{a}v_{a} = 1$; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.set-and-clear-of-a-bit-generate-the-hyperbolic-plane}) such that for $a \ne b$ each of $v_{a}, w_{a}$ anticommutes with each of $v_{b}, w_{b}$. Put $e_{a} = v_{a} + w_{a}$, $f_{a} = v_{a} - w_{a}$, $n_{a} = v_{a}w_{a}$, $h_{a} = 1 - 2n_{a}$, and
\[
u = e_{1}e_{2}\cdots e_{m} \ \ (m \text{ odd}), \qquad u = f_{1}f_{2}\cdots f_{m} \ \ (m \text{ even}), \qquad X(x) = u\,x\,u^{-1}.
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The exchange is inner.)} $u^{2} = \pm 1$, and $X(v_{a}) = w_{a}$, $X(w_{a}) = v_{a}$ for every $a$; $X^{2}$ is the identity. On the subring generated by the switches $X$ is the only ring homomorphism that exchanges set and clear in every switch.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(What it fixes.)} $X(e_{a}) = e_{a}$ and $X(f_{a}) = -f_{a}$, so for $S, S' \subseteq \{1, \dots, m\}$ the product $e_{S}f_{S'}$ of the $e_{a}$, $a \in S$, and the $f_{a}$, $a \in S'$, goes to $(-1)^{|S'|}e_{S}f_{S'}$: every blade is fixed up to sign, and $u$ is itself a blade. Hence $X$ preserves the integer span of the blades (the image of the integer Clifford algebra of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.integer-clifford-algebras-contain-no-switch}), each plane $\Z v_{a} + \Z w_{a}$ with its form $(\alpha v_{a} + \beta w_{a})^{2} = \alpha\beta$, and the parity of the number of vector factors. If $A$ has an anti-automorphism $\rho$ fixing every $v_{a}$ and $w_{a}$ (reversal), then $X\rho = \rho X$ on the subring generated by the switches, and $X\rho$ is there the anti-automorphism exchanging $v_{a}$ and $w_{a}$: the adjoint is the exchange composed with reversal.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(What it moves.)} $X(n_{a}) = 1 - n_{a}$ and $X(h_{a}) = -h_{a}$ with $h_{a} = e_{a}f_{a}$; so the number $\sum_{a}n_{a}$ goes to $m$ minus itself, $h_{1}\cdots h_{m}$ goes to $(-1)^{m}h_{1}\cdots h_{m}$, and the two idempotents $p_{\mathrm{off}} = \prod_{a}(1 - n_{a})$ and $p_{\mathrm{on}} = \prod_{a}n_{a}$ are exchanged. The volume element $h_{1}\cdots h_{m}$ is reversed exactly when $m$ is odd, which is when $u$ is a product of an odd number of the $e_{a}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(No invariant vacuum.)} If $\psi \in A$ satisfies $w_{a}\psi = 0$ for one $a$ and $X(\psi) = \psi$, then $\psi = 0$. If $q \in A$ satisfies $X(q) = -q$ and $\omega$ is an additive map from $A$ to an abelian group with $\omega \circ X = \omega$, then $2\,\omega(q) = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Integer states.)} Call an additive map $\omega : A \to \Z$ with $\omega(1) = 1$ an integer state. No integer state satisfies $\omega \circ X = \omega$, for any $m \ge 1$. If $A$ carries the adjoint $x \mapsto x^{\dagger}$ of (ii) and $\omega(v_{a}v_{a}^{\dagger}) \ge 0$, $\omega(w_{a}w_{a}^{\dagger}) \ge 0$ for all $a$, then $\omega(n_{a}) \in \{0, 1\}$ for every $a$: the state gives each switch a definite position, its charge $q(\omega) = \sum_{a}\omega(2n_{a} - 1)$ is an integer with $|q| \le m$ and $q \equiv m \pmod 2$, and $q(\omega \circ X) = -q(\omega)$. On the integer span of the ordered monomials in the $v_{a}, w_{a}$ inside $\Cl_{\Q}(m,m)$ every such value of $q$ occurs: for each configuration $\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{m}$ the map $\omega_{\sigma}(x) = 2^{m}\langle p_{\sigma}x\rangle_{0}$, $p_{\sigma} = \prod_{a}(\sigma_{a}n_{a} + (1 - \sigma_{a})(1 - n_{a}))$, is an integer state with these two properties and $\omega_{\sigma}(n_{a}) = \sigma_{a}$, and $\omega_{\sigma} \circ X = \omega_{\bar\sigma}$ for the complementary configuration.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(With one half.)} On $\Cl_{\Q}(m,m)$ the scalar part $\tau = \langle\,\cdot\,\rangle_{0}$ satisfies $\tau \circ X = \tau$ and $\tau(n_{a}) = \tfrac12$; it is integer-valued on the integer span of the blades and not on the integer span of the monomials in the $v_{a}, w_{a}$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading (argued, not proved).} The foundation's distinction between nothing and something (Premise \claimref{synthesis.premise-the-bit}) is, in the algebra, the label of a blade, the set of directions present in it, and by (ii) the exchange fixes every label. The off and on of a switch are the two signs of $h_{a} = e_{a}f_{a}$, a sign the bit does not carry and the exchange reverses. So in the order that builds directions first the two positions of a switch are not distinguished by anything the foundation holds, and an invariant value assignment exists, on an algebra that contains no switch. In the order that builds the switch first, over the integers, there is none: every integer state is oriented, and which way is a label, moved by an inner automorphism. The descent's flag (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) is the choice of the annihilated half in each of three pairs, and its conjugate is this exchange with $m = 3$, an odd number, which reverses the volume element (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}(iii)). Whether the exchange is a symmetry of the stored laws is not decided here: the algebra above is complex-linear and sees no real form, and on the conformal ambient the stored conjugation result gives the answer for the action (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}).

## technical
For any number of anticommuting set-and-clear pairs, exchanging set with clear in all of them is conjugation by a product of the pairs' directions, those of square $+1$ when the number of pairs is odd. It fixes every blade up to sign, the integer lattice of blades, the hyperbolic form and reversal, and composed with reversal it is the adjoint. It reverses each number operator about one half, exchanges the empty and the full idempotent, and reverses the volume element exactly for an odd number of pairs. Nothing annihilated by a clear operation is invariant, and no normalised integer-valued value assignment is invariant: an integer state that is positive on $vv^{\dagger}$ and $ww^{\dagger}$ puts every switch definitely on or off, with a total charge of the parity of the number of switches, and the exchange reverses that charge. The invariant assignment, the scalar part, gives each switch the value one half and is integral only on the blade lattice, which contains no switch.

## lay
Take any number of on/off switches. Swapping the meaning of on and off in all of them at once changes nothing about the rules the switches obey: the swap can be carried out by an operation already present among the rules. So the rules cannot say which position is really on. Yet if values must be whole numbers, every possible assignment of values puts each switch definitely on or definitely off, and no assignment is balanced between the two; balance needs the number one half. In that setting some imbalance between on and off is unavoidable, while which side it favours is a matter of naming. For the matter in the universe this is a statement about the starting point of the theory only: it does not show that the laws built later treat matter and antimatter alike.

## one-liner
For $m$ anticommuting switches, exchanging every set with its clear is conjugation by a blade ($e_{1}\cdots e_{m}$ for odd $m$), fixes every blade up to sign and equals the adjoint composed with reversal; it reverses the volume element exactly for odd $m$, no vacuum and no normalised integer-valued state is invariant under it, and the invariant state needs $\tfrac12$.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Preliminaries.} By the relations of a switch (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.set-and-clear-of-a-bit-generate-the-hyperbolic-plane}(i), (iv)), $e_{a}^{2} = 1$, $f_{a}^{2} = -1$, $e_{a}f_{a} = w_{a}v_{a} - v_{a}w_{a} = 1 - 2n_{a} = -f_{a}e_{a}$, and by the hypothesis on distinct switches the $2m$ elements $e_{a}, f_{a}$ pairwise anticommute. Also $e_{a}v_{a} = w_{a}v_{a}$ and $v_{a}e_{a} = v_{a}w_{a}$, so $e_{a}v_{a}e_{a} = w_{a}v_{a}w_{a} = w_{a}(1 - w_{a}v_{a}) = w_{a}$, and likewise $e_{a}w_{a}e_{a} = v_{a}$.

\emph{(i)} A product of $m$ pairwise anticommuting elements $g_{1}, \dots, g_{m}$ squares to $(-1)^{m(m-1)/2}g_{1}^{2}\cdots g_{m}^{2}$, so $u^{2} = \pm 1$ and $u^{-1} = \pm u$. Let $m$ be odd, $u = e_{1}\cdots e_{m}$. Then $e_{a}$ commutes with itself and anticommutes with the other $m - 1$ factors, an even number, so $u\,e_{a} = e_{a}u$; and $f_{a}$ anticommutes with all $m$ factors, so $u\,f_{a} = -f_{a}u$. Let $m$ be even, $u = f_{1}\cdots f_{m}$. Then $f_{a}$ anticommutes with $m - 1$ factors, an odd number, so $u\,f_{a} = -f_{a}u$, and $e_{a}$ anticommutes with all $m$, so $u\,e_{a} = e_{a}u$. In both cases $X(e_{a}) = e_{a}$ and $X(f_{a}) = -f_{a}$, that is $X(v_{a} + w_{a}) = v_{a} + w_{a}$ and $X(v_{a} - w_{a}) = w_{a} - v_{a}$. For the null vectors themselves: for $m$ odd write $u = \pm e_{a}u'$ with $u'$ the product of the other $e_{b}$, an even number of elements each anticommuting with $v_{a}$, so $u'v_{a} = v_{a}u'$ and $u\,v_{a}\,u^{-1} = e_{a}v_{a}e_{a}^{-1} = e_{a}v_{a}e_{a} = w_{a}$ by the preliminaries; likewise $X(w_{a}) = v_{a}$. For $m$ even write $u = \pm f_{a}u'$ with $u'$ the product of the other $f_{b}$, an odd number, so $u'v_{a}u'^{-1} = -v_{a}$; and $f_{a}v_{a} = -w_{a}v_{a}$, so $f_{a}v_{a}f_{a} = -w_{a}v_{a}(v_{a} - w_{a}) = w_{a}v_{a}w_{a} = w_{a}$ and $f_{a}v_{a}f_{a}^{-1} = -f_{a}v_{a}f_{a} = -w_{a}$; together $X(v_{a}) = w_{a}$, and likewise $X(w_{a}) = v_{a}$. $X^{2}$ is conjugation by $u^{2} = \pm 1$, the identity. A ring homomorphism of the subring generated by the switches is determined by its values on the generators.

\emph{(ii)} The first statement is in the proof of (i), and multiplicativity gives $X(e_{S}f_{S'}) = (-1)^{|S'|}e_{S}f_{S'}$. $u$ is $e_{S}f_{S'}$ with $S$ or $S'$ the whole index set. The integer span of the blades is the image of the integer Clifford algebra under $e_{a} \mapsto v_{a} + w_{a}$, $f_{a} \mapsto v_{a} - w_{a}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.integer-clifford-algebras-contain-no-switch}(iv) for one switch), and $X$ maps each blade to itself up to sign. $X(\alpha v_{a} + \beta w_{a}) = \beta v_{a} + \alpha w_{a}$, of the same square $\alpha\beta$. $X$ maps generators to generators, so it preserves the parity of a product of them. If $\rho$ is an anti-automorphism fixing the $v_{a}, w_{a}$, then $X\rho$ and $\rho X$ are anti-automorphisms that agree on the generators, sending $v_{a}$ to $w_{a}$ and $w_{a}$ to $v_{a}$; so they agree on the subring generated.

\emph{(iii)} $X(n_{a}) = w_{a}v_{a} = 1 - n_{a}$, so $X(h_{a}) = 2n_{a} - 1 = -h_{a}$, and the statements on the number, on $h_{1}\cdots h_{m}$ and on the two idempotents follow by additivity and multiplicativity.

\emph{(iv)} If $w_{a}\psi = 0$ and $X(\psi) = \psi$ then $v_{a}\psi = X(w_{a})X(\psi) = X(w_{a}\psi) = 0$, so $\psi = (v_{a}w_{a} + w_{a}v_{a})\psi = 0$. If $X(q) = -q$ and $\omega \circ X = \omega$ then $\omega(q) = \omega(X(q)) = -\omega(q)$.

\emph{(v)} If $\omega \circ X = \omega$ then $\omega(n_{1}) = \omega(1 - n_{1})$, so $2\,\omega(n_{1}) = \omega(1) = 1$, which no integer satisfies. With the adjoint, $v_{a}v_{a}^{\dagger} = v_{a}w_{a} = n_{a}$ and $w_{a}w_{a}^{\dagger} = w_{a}v_{a} = 1 - n_{a}$, so the two inequalities give $0 \le \omega(n_{a}) \le 1$ and $\omega(n_{a}) \in \{0, 1\}$; $q(\omega)$ is then a sum of $m$ terms $\pm 1$, and $q(\omega \circ X) = \sum_{a}\omega(1 - 2n_{a}) = -q(\omega)$. For the last statement, in $\Cl_{\Q}(m,m)$ the $n_{a}$ are commuting idempotents with $\langle p_{\sigma}\rangle_{0} = 2^{-m}$ (each factor is $\tfrac12(1 \pm e_{a}f_{a})$), so $\omega_{\sigma}(1) = 1$; $\omega_{\sigma}$ is the diagonal matrix entry at the configuration $\sigma$ in the representation on the $m$-fold product of two-state modules, in which the monomials in the $v_{a}, w_{a}$ have entries $0, \pm 1$, so it is integer-valued on their integer span; $p_{\sigma}n_{a} = \sigma_{a}p_{\sigma}$ gives $\omega_{\sigma}(n_{a}) = \sigma_{a}$ and the two inequalities; and $X(p_{\sigma}) = p_{\bar\sigma}$ with the invariance of the scalar part under conjugation gives $\omega_{\sigma} \circ X = \omega_{\bar\sigma}$. The charges $2|\sigma| - m$ run over all integers of absolute value at most $m$ and of the parity of $m$.

\emph{(vi)} The scalar part is invariant under conjugation, $n_{a} = \tfrac12(1 - e_{a}f_{a})$ has scalar part $\tfrac12$, and a blade has scalar part $0$ or $1$.

check_py:
"""synthesis.exchange-of-set-and-clear-is-inner-and-fixed-by-no-integer-state: exact checks.

m anticommuting switches are modelled in Cl(m,m) over the rationals with GA.py: generators
e_1..e_m of square +1 (indices 0..m-1), f_1..f_m of square -1 (indices m..2m-1),
v_a = (e_a + f_a)/2, w_a = (e_a - f_a)/2. The integer switch algebra is the integer span of the
ordered monomials v_S w_T inside it.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations, product

import GA
from tp_premise import premise


class Switches:
    def __init__(self, m):
        self.m = m
        self.sq = GA.sig(m, m)
        self.one = GA.sc(1)
        self.e = [GA.gen(a) for a in range(m)]
        self.f = [GA.gen(m + a) for a in range(m)]
        self.v = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(self.e[a], self.f[a])) for a in range(m)]
        self.w = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(self.e[a], self.f[a])) for a in range(m)]
        self.n = [self.mul(self.v[a], self.w[a]) for a in range(m)]
        self.u = self.mul(*(self.e if m % 2 == 1 else self.f))
        s = self.mul(self.u, self.u)
        self.uinv = GA.scal(1 / s[()], self.u)

    def mul(self, *xs):
        r = xs[0]
        for x in xs[1:]:
            r = GA.mul(r, x, self.sq)
        return r

    def X(self, x):
        return self.mul(self.u, x, self.uinv)

    def flip(self, x):
        m = self.m
        return {b: (c if sum(1 for i in b if i >= m) % 2 == 0 else -c) for b, c in x.items()}

    def dagger(self, x):
        return self.flip(GA.reverse(x))

    def monomials(self):
        subsets = [s for r in range(self.m + 1) for s in combinations(range(self.m), r)]
        return [self.mul(self.one, *[self.v[a] for a in s], *[self.w[a] for a in t])
                for s in subsets for t in subsets]

    def state(self, sigma):
        """The integer state of the configuration sigma (1 = on): x -> 2^m sc(p_sigma x)."""
        p = self.mul(self.one, *[self.n[a] if sigma[a] else GA.sub(self.one, self.n[a])
                                 for a in range(self.m)])
        return lambda x: 2 ** self.m * self.mul(p, x).get((), F(0))


def check_exchange_is_conjugation_by_a_product_of_directions():
    premise("synthesis.set-and-clear-of-a-bit-generate-the-hyperbolic-plane")
    for m in range(1, 6):
        A = Switches(m)
        for a in range(m):
            assert A.mul(A.v[a], A.v[a]) == {} and A.mul(A.w[a], A.w[a]) == {}
            assert GA.add(A.mul(A.v[a], A.w[a]), A.mul(A.w[a], A.v[a])) == A.one
            assert A.mul(A.e[a], A.e[a]) == A.one and A.mul(A.f[a], A.f[a]) == GA.neg(A.one)
            for b in range(m):
                if a != b:
                    assert GA.anticommutes(A.v[a], A.v[b], A.sq) and GA.anticommutes(A.v[a], A.w[b], A.sq)
        uu = A.mul(A.u, A.u)
        sign = (-1) ** (m * (m - 1) // 2) if m % 2 == 1 else (-1) ** (m // 2)
        assert uu == GA.sc(sign)
        for a in range(m):
            assert GA.eq(A.X(A.v[a]), A.w[a]) and GA.eq(A.X(A.w[a]), A.v[a])
            assert GA.eq(A.X(A.e[a]), A.e[a]) and GA.eq(A.X(A.f[a]), GA.neg(A.f[a]))
            assert GA.eq(A.X(A.X(A.v[a])), A.v[a])
        # the other product of directions does not exchange: it sends v_a to -w_a
        other = A.mul(*(A.f if m % 2 == 1 else A.e))
        oinv = GA.scal(1 / A.mul(other, other)[()], other)
        assert GA.eq(A.mul(other, A.v[0], oinv), GA.neg(A.w[0]))
    return True


def check_what_the_exchange_fixes():
    premise("synthesis.set-and-clear-of-a-bit-generate-the-hyperbolic-plane")
    premise("synthesis.integer-clifford-algebras-contain-no-switch")
    for m in range(1, 4):
        A = Switches(m)
        # every blade e_S f_T goes to (-1)^|T| times itself: the configuration is fixed
        for blade in GA.all_blades(2 * m):
            x = {blade: F(1)}
            t = sum(1 for i in blade if i >= m)
            assert GA.eq(A.X(x), GA.scal((-1) ** t, x))
            assert GA.eq(A.X(x), A.flip(x))
        # the implementer is a blade, an element of the integer ladder algebra
        assert len(A.u) == 1 and set(A.u.values()) == {F(1)}
        # the hyperbolic form on each plane
        for a in range(m):
            for al, be in product(range(-3, 4), repeat=2):
                x = GA.add(GA.scal(al, A.v[a]), GA.scal(be, A.w[a]))
                assert A.mul(x, x) == GA.sc(al * be)
                assert A.mul(A.X(x), A.X(x)) == GA.sc(al * be)
        # reversal commutes with the exchange; adjoint = exchange after reversal, an anti-automorphism
        mons = A.monomials()
        assert len(mons) == 4 ** m
        for x in mons:
            assert GA.eq(A.X(GA.reverse(x)), GA.reverse(A.X(x)))
            assert GA.eq(A.X(GA.grade_inv(x)), GA.grade_inv(A.X(x)))
        for a in range(m):
            assert GA.eq(A.dagger(A.v[a]), A.w[a]) and GA.eq(A.dagger(A.w[a]), A.v[a])
        x, y = mons[3], mons[-2]
        assert GA.eq(A.dagger(A.mul(x, y)), A.mul(A.dagger(y), A.dagger(x)))
    return True


def check_what_the_exchange_moves():
    premise("synthesis.set-and-clear-of-a-bit-generate-the-hyperbolic-plane")
    for m in range(1, 6):
        A = Switches(m)
        h = [GA.sub(A.one, GA.scal(2, A.n[a])) for a in range(m)]
        for a in range(m):
            assert GA.eq(h[a], A.mul(A.e[a], A.f[a]))
            assert GA.eq(A.X(A.n[a]), GA.sub(A.one, A.n[a]))
            assert GA.eq(A.X(h[a]), GA.neg(h[a]))
        number = GA.add(*A.n)
        assert GA.eq(A.X(number), GA.sub(GA.sc(m), number))
        omega = A.mul(*h)
        assert GA.eq(A.X(omega), GA.scal((-1) ** m, omega))
        p_off = A.mul(A.one, *[GA.sub(A.one, A.n[a]) for a in range(m)])
        p_on = A.mul(A.one, *A.n)
        assert GA.eq(A.X(p_off), p_on) and GA.eq(A.X(p_on), p_off) and not GA.eq(p_off, p_on)
        for a in range(m):
            assert A.mul(A.w[a], p_off) == {} and A.mul(A.v[a], p_on) == {}
            assert A.mul(A.v[a], p_off) != {}
    return True


def check_integer_states_choose_an_orientation():
    premise("synthesis.set-and-clear-of-a-bit-generate-the-hyperbolic-plane")
    premise("synthesis.integer-clifford-algebras-contain-no-switch")
    for m in range(1, 4):
        A = Switches(m)
        mons = A.monomials()
        charges = set()
        for sigma in product((0, 1), repeat=m):
            st = A.state(sigma)
            assert st(A.one) == 1
            assert all(st(x) in (0, 1, -1) for x in mons)          # integer on the integer span
            for a in range(m):
                assert st(A.n[a]) == sigma[a]
                assert st(A.mul(A.v[a], A.dagger(A.v[a]))) == sigma[a]
                assert st(A.mul(A.w[a], A.dagger(A.w[a]))) == 1 - sigma[a]
            q = sum(st(GA.sub(GA.scal(2, A.n[a]), A.one)) for a in range(m))
            assert q == 2 * sum(sigma) - m and (q - m) % 2 == 0
            bar = A.state(tuple(1 - s for s in sigma))
            assert all(st(A.X(x)) == bar(x) for x in mons)          # the exchange reverses the charge
            charges.add(q)
        assert charges == set(range(-m, m + 1, 2))
        assert (0 in charges) == (m % 2 == 0)
        # the scalar part is exchange-invariant, takes the value 1/2 on each n_a, and is integral
        # on the blades (the integer ladder algebra) but not on the integer switch algebra
        tau = lambda x: x.get((), F(0))
        assert all(tau(A.X(x)) == tau(x) for x in mons)
        assert all(2 * tau(A.n[a]) == 1 for a in range(m))
        assert all(tau({b: F(1)}) in (0, 1) for b in GA.all_blades(2 * m))
    return True
